consumer: The engine condition/dialogue check built by conditional_t::set_has_items for u_has_items, asking 'does the avatar actor hold >=30 of 9mm?' as a computed yes/no.
scope: only the character's own carried items (on-person inventory, including ammo nested in worn/wielded containers, magazines, and guns)
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_items — its body returns actor->has_charges(item_id,count) || actor->has_amount(item_id,count) over the character actor, i.e. an engine-computed boolean over the avatar's own held items, exactly the threshold authority the goal needs.
divergence: Avatar wields a 9mm pistol with a loaded 30-round magazine (and nothing loose). has_charges/has_amount returns true (>=30), but a re-derivation summing only top-level carried_items[].charges from write_carried_items misses rounds nested inside the gun/magazine and answers 'no' — exposing the wrong authority.
